steps.description: Choose appropriate tool: pandas for data inspection, openpyxl for formulas/formatting
Load existing workbook and inspect all sheets

failure_patterns.reason: ⚠️ Never save a workbook loaded with data_only=True — all formulas will be permanently replaced with cached static values.

suggestions: Inspect the workbook structure first: read all sheet names, check which cells are empty, and understand the expected output regions before writing.

steps.description: Step 1 — Fill expression data cells with lookup formulas (100+ cells required)

suggestions: Fill all target expression cells with formulas — the verifier requires at least 80/100 cells to be filled.
Use INDEX/MATCH or VLOOKUP to look up values from the source data sheet by protein name and sample ID.
warnings: Do NOT leave expression data cells empty — '0/100 cells filled' is the most common failure mode. Every target cell must have a formula or value.

failure_patterns.reason: ❌ Never write None to expression data cells — they must contain numeric values or lookup formulas. None leaves cells empty and fails the fill check.

steps.description: Step 2 — Calculate statistics (mean, std, CV) for each protein across samples

suggestions: Statistics formulas (AVERAGE, STDEV) must reference the filled expression range — write them AFTER the expression data is in place.

steps.description: Step 3 — Calculate fold changes relative to control condition

suggestions: Fold change = treatment_value / control_value. Use absolute cell references ($) for the control column.

steps.description: Recalculate formulas using recalc.py (mandatory when formulas are used)
Verify all cells are populated — check expression (80+/100), statistics (32+), fold changes (8+)

suggestions: After recalc, verify with data_only=True that expression cells, statistics cells, and fold change cells all contain numeric values.
Check recalc.py JSON: 'status: success' and 'total_errors: 0' before finishing.
